records.supported_name_scope: Lloyds River is directly labeled on the eastward wetland connection near Andrews Pond and on the northeastward corridor through Lloyds Lake toward Beothuk Lake. The three lake names are supported as lake components. Exploits River is directly labeled downstream of Beothuk Lake and along the selected lower river through the Badger and Bishop’s Falls settings.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection approaches from the marshy country southwest of Andrews Pond, then takes the eastward Lloyds River connection into King George IV Lake. It does not use the more southerly Finger Pond–Princess Lake route. It continues northeast through Lloyds Lake, west of the distinct Victoria Lake and Victoria River system, into the southwestern end of Beothuk Lake. After crossing that lake it follows Exploits River from Millertown past Badger, turns east toward Grand Falls–Windsor, and then northeast past Bishop’s Falls. Its endpoint is on the lower Exploits southwest of Rattling Brook, at the approach to the broad inlet extending toward Norris Arm and Botwood.
records.region: Central Newfoundland, from the southwestern Lloyds headwater country northeast through Beothuk Lake, Millertown, Badger, Grand Falls–Windsor and Bishop’s Falls.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected southwestern headward approach, Lloyds River and its lake reaches, Beothuk Lake, and the lower Exploits River.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded river-corridor correspondence for all three selected mainstem fragments using four original Canada Base Map raster exports. A full-route view and overlapping upper and lower enlargements cover the complete selection. A final small southwestern enlargement resolves the labeled eastward Lloyds connection near Andrews Pond and its entrance to King George IV Lake. Original map pixels were inspected separately from orientation overlays. This establishes generalized waterway, lake and junction correspondence, not exact channel banks, every wetland thread, an official river source point or a uniform name for the complete modeled route.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Small southwestern marsh-and-stream approach southwest of Andrews Pond; a separate watercourse name is not established.
naming_scope_details.upper_named_component: Lloyds River, including the selected eastward wetland connection near Andrews Pond and northeastward river corridor.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Exploits River downstream of Beothuk Lake.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Exploits River southwest of Rattling Brook, approaching the broad inlet toward Norris Arm and Botwood.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Exploits River uniformly to Lloyds River, the lake passages or the unnamed initial approach.
The selected eastward wetland connection is distinguished from the southerly Finger Pond–Princess Lake route and from Victoria River and Victoria Lake.
No official source point, exact wetland channel thread, exhaustive tributary inventory, alternative Indigenous river name or Korean name is established.
Beothuk Lake is the name read on the inspected map; a formal naming decision date or historical-name equivalence is not inferred.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 288.89 km modeled length is the length of this three-fragment selection, not an official length of Exploits River or Lloyds River. The retained route generalizes lake crossings, wetlands, meanders and the terminal approach; no geometry change is proposed.

records.supported_name_scope: Original map labels support Rivière Aguanish Nord-Ouest for the upper named corridor, Rivière Aguanish Nord below Lac aux Deux Loutres, and Rivière Aguanish below their receiving junction. Selected lake passages include the southeastern Lac Duboys setting, Lac Uatnakantuk, the Lac Harvey setting, Lac aux Deux Loutres and Lac Padoue. The first small southwestern lake-and-stream approach has no separately established name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The initial selected route bends east and north through small lakes southwest of Lac Duboys, reaches that lake's southeastern part, and then turns east into the Aguanish Nord-Ouest corridor. It crosses Lac Uatnakantuk, continues southeast and south through the Lac Harvey setting, then turns east along Lac aux Deux Loutres. From the eastern lake outlet it follows Lac Padoue and Aguanish Nord south to the Aguanish river arriving from the west. The combined river runs southeast and then generally south, before turning southwest toward Aguanish on the coast. The route is distinct from the unselected northern continuation of Aguanish Nord above Lac aux Deux Loutres, the western upper Aguanish, and the neighboring Nabisipi coastal drainage.
records.region: Québec Côte-Nord, from the Lac Duboys headward setting southeast through the Aguanish northern branches to the Aguanish coastal setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected western headward lake approach, Aguanish Nord-Ouest, Aguanish Nord and lower Aguanish route.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded river-corridor correspondence for both selected mainstem fragments against two original Canada Base Map raster exports. The whole-route raster covers the complete selection; the northern enlargement resolves the initial lake-and-stream connection, southeastern Lac Duboys passage and connection to the named northwest branch. Original map pixels were inspected separately from local orientation overlays over the headward approach, both northern branches, named lake passages, receiving junction, lower river and terminal setting. Requested geographic extents and raster aspect ratios agree. This establishes generalized waterway, lake and junction correspondence, not exact banks, an official source point, exhaustive minor names or point-by-point alignment.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Small southwestern lake-and-stream approach to the southeastern Lac Duboys setting; separate initial names not established.
naming_scope_details.intermediate_named_component: Rivière Aguanish Nord below Lac aux Deux Loutres and through the Lac Padoue setting.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Rivière Aguanish below its junction with Aguanish Nord.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Aguanish river-mouth setting immediately inland of the coastal road at Aguanish.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Rivière Aguanish uniformly to Aguanish Nord-Ouest, Aguanish Nord, the lake passages or the initially unnamed approach.
Do not substitute the separate western upper Aguanish corridor or the northern Aguanish Nord approach above Lac aux Deux Loutres for the selected branch sequence.
The initial small water bodies and stream have no separately established names in this finding. The modeled starting vertex is not asserted to be an official river source.
The review does not establish every minor water-body name, an alternative Indigenous name for the river system, a legal naming date or a Korean name. No Canadian gazetteer or CGN records were used.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 287.915 km modeled length describes this selected two-fragment route, not an official length for Aguanish or either northern branch. The retained line generalizes lakes, meanders, small channels and the river-mouth setting. The terminal vertex is not an exact shoreline point. No geometry change is proposed.

records.supported_name_scope: East Fork Amite River is the selected upper branch. Amite River applies below the fork junction through the lower river to Lake Maurepas. The selection crosses Lake Maurepas, takes the southern inter-lake channel labeled Pass Manchac, then crosses Lake Pontchartrain. The sole modeled tributary is an open-water link entirely within Lake Pontchartrain and has no separately established watercourse name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The northern selection follows East Fork Amite west of McComb, rather than the neighboring Tangipahoa drainage or the western Amite fork. It joins the main Amite near the Mississippi–Louisiana boundary, continues south past the Denham Springs setting and turns east along the lower Amite to Lake Maurepas. The lake-to-lake passage is Pass Manchac, south of the distinct North Pass. The terminal lake route approaches The Rigolets near Pike Fort and ends lakeward of the US 90 bridge; it does not traverse the full Rigolets channel or reach Lake Borgne.
records.region: Southwestern Mississippi and southeastern Louisiana, from the East Fork Amite corridor west of McComb through the Amite valley to Lakes Maurepas and Pontchartrain.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative identity of the named river portion of a modeled system that also includes East Fork Amite River, two lakes and an inter-lake pass.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence for all four selected fragments using original federal raster maps: a full-route view plus inter-lake and terminal enlargements. Original pixels and separate local orientation overlays were inspected for the headward branch, fork junction, entire Amite valley, river entrance into Maurepas, lake crossings, selected pass, lake-internal tributary and terminal setting. This establishes generalized route and waterbody correspondence, not exact banks, an official river source, navigation conditions or a uniform river name for modeled lake links.

naming_scope_details.main_river_component: Amite River below the fork junction and through its western Lake Maurepas entrance.
naming_scope_details.selected_tributary_scope: Lake-internal modeled link within Lake Pontchartrain; no landward tributary correspondence or separate channel name is established.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lake Pontchartrain's western approach to The Rigolets, lakeward of the US 90 bridge near Pike Fort.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Amite River uniformly to East Fork Amite River, either lake, Pass Manchac or the lake-internal modeled branch.
Do not substitute North Pass for the selected Pass Manchac, or infer a traversal of the full Rigolets channel, Lake Saint Catherine, Lake Borgne or the Mississippi Sound.

The source service has scale-dependent river-label placement over lake or pass waters. The detailed Pass Manchac label and actual waterbody footprints control the component finding; isolated Amite or Tchefuncte labels over open water do not rename the modeled lake links.
No official source point, exhaustive tributary list, Korean form, historical naming decision or exact legal name boundary is inferred.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The retained 287.286 km mainstem and 294.458 km network lengths describe this modeled river–lake–pass route, not an official length of the Amite River. Straight lake links and generalized meanders are retained without geometry changes.

records.supported_name_scope: Repeated Kuparuk River labels support the upper northward/northwestward river corridor and the lower northeastward/northward receiving river. Gwydyr Bay is directly labeled at the selected coastal terminal. The unnamed initial approach, the western middle streams and individual delta channels are not assigned the Kuparuk name uniformly.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected headward end lies on a short northern approach immediately above the east-to-west upper Kuparuk bend, east of Toolik Lake and north of the Atigun valley setting. It turns north, crosses the Dalton Highway and continues northwest along the named Kuparuk corridor, with Itkillik separate to the west and Toolik River separate to the east. In the middle coastal-plain reach, the model departs west of the distinctly mapped braided Kuparuk and runs along or near smaller western streams before turning east/northeast toward the mapped lower Kuparuk. The lower selected corridor is again repeatedly labeled Kuparuk, continuing north east of the separate Sakonowyak drainage. Its terminal tail passes through the Kuparuk delta setting and ends in mapped Gwydyr Bay. Those observations do not supply a continuous source-backed connection through the entire western middle departure.
records.region: Alaska North Slope, from the upper Kuparuk country near the Dalton Highway north through the coastal plain to Gwydyr Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity supported for the named upper and lower corridors; not a uniform name for the entire selected line.
records.completion_scope: Four original National Map raster exports were acquired and inspected: whole selection, headward detail, terminal detail and a middle-reach enlargement. The inspection establishes the representative Kuparuk identity, the short unnamed initial approach and the bay terminal, and exposes an actual middle-route correspondence gap. It does not complete the whole feature. A locally fitted orientation overlay was kept separate from original source pixels; source labels and waterways were read from the originals. No river geometry was changed or revalidated.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected western middle interval and its transitions are not continuously matched to the named main Kuparuk channel or to a connected alternative watercourse in the inspected detailed cartography. A further independently permissible primary source would be needed to establish that actual selected-route correspondence. The supported upper/lower Kuparuk identity and readable Gwydyr Bay terminal cannot substitute for this missing middle correspondence.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Short unnamed northern approach near the east-to-west upper Kuparuk bend; mapped connection to the north-running upper corridor is visible, but no official source point is inferred.
naming_scope_details.middle_component: Unresolved western departure alongside smaller streams and lakes, west of the distinctly mapped main Kuparuk channel.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Kuparuk delta setting followed by a modeled tail into Gwydyr Bay.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Kuparuk River uniformly to the unnamed initial approach, unresolved western middle interval, individual delta arms or open-bay tail.
Do not replace the selected western middle interval with the better-labeled Kuparuk channel to its east and then claim complete correspondence.
Do not infer a separate name, official source point, historical course, channel avulsion, or reason for the model/source difference.
No Indigenous alternative, formal naming date or Korean name is established by these map pixels.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The retained 286.454 km is the modeled selected-route length, not an official Kuparuk River length. The line generalizes channels and meanders and includes a terminal bay extension. Its substantial middle departure remains unresolved; no geometry correction or revalidation is proposed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
